title: Official Translations of Names of New Places
what_it_is: Official Translations of Names of New Places

sections.label: Street and building name translations
sections.summary: Chinese translations of approved English street names are proposed by the Ministry of Communications and Information, while no official translations are made for building and estate names.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For street names, applications are made in English.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Chinese translations of the approved English street names are then proposed by the Ministry of Communications and Information, in consultation with the National Translation Committee's Chinese Resource Panel, as necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For building and estate names, no official translations are made.

sections.label: Chinese street name translation history
sections.summary: A committee set up in 1968 standardised Chinese street names, a practice that continues, while no official Malay and Tamil translations are made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the past, we had street names in English and Malay, but the various Chinese dialect groups had their own dialect versions of the names.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That was why in 1968, the then-Ministry of Culture decided to set up a committee to standardise the Chinese names and this committee went about doing so, and that practice of providing official translations of street names in Chinese has continued till today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do not do so for Malay and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have not done so in the past and we still do not do so because the issue of different translations did not arise in these languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, Jalan Bukit Merah which is in Malay, and Neythal Road which is in Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But there was a necessity to do so in Mandarin for the reasons I have explained earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as I have stated in my reply, the names in English and Mandarin are all available on the URA website.
